cases.attack: general, compute-intensive foundation architectures can create large capability despite high orchestration/infrastructure cost
cases.reading: Generality and scale can repay large overhead in some regimes, so S6/R8 cannot be read as narrow/local/simple always wins; repayment is objective-, horizon- and ecosystem-relative.

cases.attack: dramatic component cost decline may fail to solve the system once grid/flexibility interfaces become the bottleneck
cases.reading: Local component progress can be real and enormous while the governing system problem migrates. Generalization must bind the system boundary and current bottleneck.

cases.attack: a decisive physical ignition result may still be far from a realizable energy system
cases.reading: Strong validation at one physical layer does not entail engineering realization, repeatability, plant efficiency or economics; validation standing is layer-specific.

cases.attack: substantial technical achievement may coexist with failure of the commercial service objective
cases.reading: The frozen breadth control establishes technical accomplishment plus commercial-objective shutdown, enough to attack one-dimensional success language but not enough for a causal S1-S10 contradiction or option-value claim.

cases.attack: deliberate parallel providers can be rational despite duplicated cost when continuity and high-consequence dependency matter
cases.reading: The frozen control establishes parallel Commercial Crew providers, but its lightweight source depth is insufficient to infer the economics or high-consequence redundancy mechanism. It remains an anti-monotone breadth probe only.

interpretation: Three thick anti-cases (A03/A07/A11) materially narrow monotone readings. F01/P02 remain breadth pressure only because their source contracts are intentionally thin. No properly scoped S1-S10 claim receives an adjudicated direct contradiction.
